harsh_interrogation_findings.question: Could Option α over-block legitimate flows that aren't in the current whitelist?
harsh_interrogation_findings.answer: Yes by design. BA's spec 5.2.3 quote (verbatim verified at line 302) makes one orchestrator-blessed auto-bulk commit the ONLY in-cycle commit permitted. The user commits from their own terminal (not routed through Bash → not gated). BA explicitly forbids dev from adding CLAUDE_INTERACTIVE_OK or any new env-var bypass (ba-spec line 240). This is correct application of spec letter.

harsh_interrogation_findings.question: Will Option α prevent the ORCHESTRATOR ITSELF from committing in this very session?
harsh_interrogation_findings.answer: Yes, intentionally. ba-spec line 241 'DO NOT commit your changes via Bash — let the user handle commit.' Spec Section 6 Gap D and 5.2.3 line 302 establish 'user commits from their own terminal' as the by-design path. No one-time bypass is needed — the user's terminal Bash is not Claude's Bash tool.

harsh_interrogation_findings.question: Could BA have over-fitted the recommendation to the b5d447e shape, missing other regression patterns?
harsh_interrogation_findings.answer: No. AC-E1 uses 'random fix' commit message (not b5d447e-specific shape), proving the hook blocks ANY non-blessed commit. AC-E3 covers push with no shape constraint. AC-E4 replays the full Cycle 2 AC7 matrix. The spec covers commit/push/merge/reset-hard — the four primary git mutations. No obvious gap in coverage.

harsh_interrogation_findings.question: Does Option α leave any path for b5d447e to recur?
harsh_interrogation_findings.answer: No path identified. b5d447e shape: chore(claude): sync ... commit message + git push origin master. Always-on hook: catches commit (message doesn't match BLESSED_BRIDGE_RE), AND catches push (unconditional block). Both arms fire. The user's terminal is the only remaining commit path — that's the spec's intended design (5.2.3).
